title: Independent teacher-assessed evidence rubric — Add and Subtract Within 10
scope: Independent educator assessment design, not original copyrighted worksheet or claim about actual class completion

sourceTaskMap.source: Warm-up (15 minutes): What Do You Know About Math?
evidence: Learner contributes a math-related idea or responds to another student's reasoning
Teacher records participation/ideas without enforcing one correct sentence
Number cards are drawn two at a time and represented by an addition or subtraction expression
Student records the resulting target within 0..10 and writes the expression against it
Multiple distinct expressions for one target are admissible
Reaching 0 is possible through equal-value subtraction such as 9 - 9
Partner explains or demonstrates how the expression produces the checked value
Number Cards (0–10) and connecting cubes/counters are optional tools, not mandatory for every fact
partialMachineChecks: Parse student-authored expression with exactly two integer operands between 0 and 10 and one + or - operation
Check arithmetic result equals the indicated board target in 0..10
Record all equivalent valid expressions rather than requiring a single string match
Store student choice of cards / expression / outcome in a reviewable record
sourceTaskMap.notYetImplementedInRuntime: Machine-validatable expression-record board and teacher sign-off are a design contract here only; no runtime expression-response capture is yet connected

evidence: Correctly match addition/subtraction expressions with numerical values
Identify every displayed addition expression whose sum is 10
Describe at least one meaningful numerical pattern in sums of 10 rather than only answering yes/no
partialMachineChecks: Numerical expression matching and recognize-ten question families
sourceTaskMap.notYetImplementedInRuntime: Teacher/student open-ended pattern explanation and source addition-table visual are not implemented as an independently scored activity

sourceTaskMap.source: Lesson synthesis (10 minutes): Math Community poster
evidence: Class discusses mathematical ideas and records them in a joint chart
Teacher facilitates rather than claims an auto-generated quiz demonstrates community norms
Official cool-down requires educator login; content has not been accessed or invented

blocking: Original Activity 2 addition-table visual was not independently inspected.
Original authenticated Cool-down text is not available to verify.
Runtime authored-expression record board and checking of multiple equivalent expressions not implemented.
Math Community/partner reasoning are teacher-assessed, not evidenced as implemented classroom assessment in Edulytics.
